notes: **2026-09-02 (concurrency + safety pass — answering the second refuter run)** — (branch `feat/bug-registry`, PR #597; `scripts/campaign/bugs.mjs` + `scripts/team/team.mjs` + SKILL.md, 5 fix commits, one per cluster of the adversarial pass that REFUTED the lock introduced in the note below, plus one test commit; self-test 129 → 181 checks) — **THE LOCK WAS BROKEN ON AGE, WHICH IS NOT LIVENESS — AND FOUR MORE.** (1) LOCK: `LOCK_STALE_MS = 5000` meant a lock older than 5s was rm'd and taken with no check that its holder was still running, so a LIVE writer whose critical section outlived 5s had its lock stolen and then wrote its stale snapshot back over two proven, evidence-backed rows — every process exiting 0, both gates green; worse, `releaseShardLock` and the exit hook rm'd the lock PATH unconditionally, so the stolen-from process went on to delete its SUCCESSOR's lock and admit a THIRD writer. A lock is now broken ONLY on its owner being DEAD: every lockdir carries `owner.json` = `{pid, token, at}` written immediately after the winning `mkdir`, a waiter breaks it when `process.kill(pid, 0)` reports ESRCH (which answers on win32 too), and AGE decides nothing except as a loud LAST RESORT (`LOCK_ABANDON_MS = 120000`) for a lockdir carrying no readable `owner.json` at all — a live pid is never broken on age, at any age. Release is identity-checked against that token: a process whose lock was broken leaves the directory alone and prints `bugs: our lock on F##.jsonl was broken by another process; verify the shard`. `LOCK_SPIN_MS` 2000 → 10000, because it was BELOW the old stale threshold — a waiter always gave up before it could reach the break, so a SIGKILLed writer's lock was never recovered in one invocation and the give-up message falsely blamed a running process. SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP are routed through `process.exit(130/143/129)`: Node's default action for those three skips `exit` listeners entirely, so a Ctrl-C mid-write used to leave the lockdir behind. (2) CATALOGUE RACE: `file` allocated its id from catalogue ∪ shards and wrote `bugs.jsonl` with NO lock at all, so two simultaneous `file --batch F01` both allocated B2, both exited 0 printing `filed B2`, and one entire bug — catalogue row, ledger row and record — vanished into a state so self-consistent that neither gate could see it. New `withCatalogueLock` over `bugs.jsonl.lock` uses the SAME primitive (a second hand-rolled copy is exactly how the two would drift) and `file` holds it from the id allocation THROUGH the catalogue write; the ledger write passes `{ mustBeNew: true }` so an id just allocated as fresh can never silently take the update branch. Lock order is one-way: catalogue, then shard. (3) CARVE-OUT OCCUPANCY: the sensitive test ran FIRST in `selectBatches` and `continue`d, so a parked batch that was in-flight or under a live lease never got `busy: true` — it occupied no slot of the agent cap, every hard conflict it carried was dropped from the colouring, and `next` offered the batch editing the SAME non-hub file to a second agent (reproduced from both the local in-flight path and a live lease). Parking is now a LABEL: busy-ness is computed BEFORE parking and a batch that is both lands in `parked` AND in the busy set that pre-colours wave 1. (4) SHELL INJECTION: `liveClaim` interpolated the `board.json` issue value into an `execSync` template string — on win32 that is cmd.exe, and a crafted board card EXECUTED. New `boardIssue()` validates at the boundary (`/^[1-9]d*$/` over the trimmed string; anything else falls into the honest `no board card for F##` branch, which also kills `next`'s `(issue #[object Object])` claim instruction), and the fetch moved to `execFileSync("gh", [...])` — no shell, ever. (5) PAGINATION BLINDNESS: both readers asked for `per_page=100` with no `--paginate`, so gh returned page 1 — the OLDEST 100 comments — while a claim is by construction the NEWEST; a lease posted as comment #101 was invisible to BOTH, and the batch occupied no capacity. Fixed in ONE commit in both files per the shared-grammar rule: `--paginate --slurp` with the array-of-pages flattened by the same expression (⚠️ `--slurp` cannot be combined with `--jq` — gh rejects the pair — so the projection happens in JS), and `readClaims` now carries each comment's server-assigned id and sorts ASCENDING so the LOWEST live claim wins, byte-mirroring `team.mjs`'s compare-and-swap (this file took API order and named a different holder). Every fix drives the REAL command through the `BUGS_ROOT`/child-process seams and would have FAILED before it: a live holder past the old 5s threshold whose waiter waits (both rows land, neither reverted), a SIGKILLed holder broken by the NEXT waiter in ONE invocation, a hand-written successor token that makes release refuse and leave the directory, a lockdir with no `owner.json` broken only as LAST RESORT, two concurrent `file` calls that must be given DISTINCT ids with both records on disk, a parked-and-busy batch from both the in-flight and lease directions, a hostile `board.json` whose marker never appears in any output, and a 101-comment fixture whose lease is only visible once the pages are joined. The `BUGS_TEST_STALL_MS` seam is now GATED on `BUGS_SELF_TEST=1` and capped at 30s — unguarded and uncapped it was honoured by every production ledger write inside the lock, i.e. a one-env-var route to the theft above rather than merely a slow write. || History in CHANGELOG.md (this directory).
